extracted.intended_audience: Area Chairs / meta-reviewers for ACL Rolling Review (ARR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for Area Chairs on writing meta-reviews: how to summarize the paper and reviews, reconcile reviewer disagreements, record post-rebuttal changes, justify accept/reject recommendations, and assess review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review purpose and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-reviews are the most crucial aspect of the review process, where the Area Chair justifies their recommendation to accept or reject a paper. The golden rule is to write meta-reviews in a way that you, as an author, would appreciate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify the accept/reject recommendation clearly and write respectfully and helpfully from an author-facing perspective. The meta-review should explain why the decision was reached rather than merely state it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of the paper: Including its strengths and weaknesses, with comments regarding novelty, significance, and relevance/impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise statement of the paper's contributions and an honest account of main strengths and weaknesses, explicitly mentioning aspects such as novelty, significance, and expected impact or relevance to the venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of post-rebuttal discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of post-rebuttal discussion: Did reviewers engage in discussion or not, did their opinion change, did they change their score?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether reviewers discussed the paper after rebuttal, summarize salient points of that discussion, and note any changes in reviewer opinions or numeric scores to show how the decision evolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback for rejection cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback for rejection cases: Give authors feedback to improve the paper, and suggestions about the next appropriate venue to submit their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending rejection, provide constructive, actionable advice for improvement and, where appropriate, recommend alternative venues that might be a better fit for the revised work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the meta-reviewer vs reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: You are an area chair because you are an expert in the field; you do not have to simply average across reviewer scores and summarize their comments. However, meta-reviewers are not reviewers (obviously), so you should avoid using only your opinion. It is not your job to write a fourth review of the paper. Instead, the goal of the meta-review is primarily to reconcile and adjudicate the reviewers' views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your expertise to adjudicate disagreements and synthesize reviewer evidence, but ground conclusions in the reviewers' evaluations and discussions rather than producing a new, independent review. Avoid replacing or overriding reviewer substance with unsupported personal opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation structure — summarize contributions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin the recommendation by clearly articulating what the paper claims to contribute, so readers of the meta-review immediately understand the core ideas being judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation structure — synthesize reviewer concerns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate and explain the main technical or presentation concerns raised by reviewers, showing how they relate to one another and to the decision being recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation structure — note how authors addressed concerns in rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: Note how authors addressed concerns in rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state which reviewer concerns were addressed satisfactorily in the rebuttal, which were not, and whether the rebuttal changed the balance of evidence for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation structure — make recommendation with justification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state accept/reject (or other recommendation) and provide the reasoning tying reviewer evidence, discussion, and rebuttal outcomes to that recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation structure — provide constructive feedback for the authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide constructive feedback for the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include actionable suggestions for improving the paper regardless of decision; feedback should be clear, specific, and useful for revision or submission elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess review quality and request revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Area chairs are also responsible for assessing the quality of the reviews themselves, requesting revisions or replacement if reviews are inadequate, terse, or unprofessional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reviewer reports for thoroughness and professionalism. If reviews are low-quality (e.g., too terse, missing justification, or unprofessional), request that reviewers revise their reports or assign a replacement reviewer so that decisions are based on adequate evidence.
